body.text:
Stage director
Chamberlain:
Badarayana, a servant of Duryodhana
Duryodhana: eldest son of Dhrtarastra
Vasudeva: Krsna, incarnation of Visnu
Sudarsana: Vasudeva's discus
Dhrtarastra: king of Hastinapura
body.translated_text: Stage director; Chamberlain: <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, a servant of <s>Duryodhana</s>; <s>Duryodhana</s>: eldest son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>; <s>Vāsudeva</s>: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, incarnation of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; <s>Sudarśana</s>: <s>Vāsudeva's</s> discus; <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>: king of <s>Hāstinapura</s>
The Envoy's Message. After the benedictory verse (<s>nāndī</s>), the stage director enters.

body.text:
sūtradhāraḥ
pādaḥ pāyādupendrasya sarvalokotsavaḥ sa vaḥ|
vyāviddho namuciryena tanutāmranakhena khe|| 1||
body.translated_text: Stage Director: May the foot of <s>Upendra</s> (Viṣṇu) protect you — that [foot] which is a festival for all the worlds, by which <s>Namuci</s> was struck down in the sky with a slender, copper-nailed [toe]. (Verse 1)

body.text:
evamāryamiśrān vijñāpayāmi| aye kiṃ nu khalu mayi vijñāpanavyagre śabda iva
śrūyate| aṅga
paśyāmi|
body.translated_text: Thus I inform the noble assembly. But what is this? While I am busy with my announcement, a sound seems to be heard. Let me see.
Offstage:

body.text: bho bhoḥ pratihārādhikṛtāḥ mahārājo duryodhanaḥ samājñāpayati|
body.translated_text: Ho there, officers of the gate! The great king <s>Duryodhana</s> commands!
Stage Director:
Very well, it is understood.

body.text:
utpanne dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ virodhe pāṇḍavaiḥ saha|
mantraśālāṃ racayati bhṛtyo duryodhanājñayā|| 2||
body.translated_text: When a conflict has arisen between the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> and the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, a servant, by order of <s>Duryodhana</s>, prepares the council hall. (Verse 2)

body.text: niṣkrāntaḥ| sthāpanā| tataḥ praviśati kāñcukīyaḥ| kāñcukīyaḥ
body.translated_text: He exits. Interlude. Then the chamberlain enters. Chamberlain:

body.text:
bho bhoḥ pratihārādhikṛtāḥ mahārājo duryodhanaḥ samājñāpayati| adya
sarvapārthivaiḥ saha
mantrayitumicchāmi| tadāhūyantāṃ sarve rājāna iti|parikramyāvalokya|aye ayaṃ
mahārājo
duryodhana ita evābhivartate| ya eṣaḥ
body.translated_text: Ho there, officers of the gate! The great king <s>Duryodhana</s> commands: 'Today I wish to take counsel with all the kings. Therefore, let all the kings be summoned.' (Walking around and looking) Ah, here comes the great king <s>Duryodhana</s> himself, approaching from this direction. He who is —

body.text:
śyāmo yuvā sitadukūlakṛtottarīyaḥ sacchattracāmaravaro racitāṅgarāgaḥ|
śrīmānvibhūṣaṇamaṇidyutirañjitāṅgo nakṣatramadhya iva parvagataḥ śaśāṅkaḥ|| 3||
body.translated_text: dark-complexioned, youthful, wearing a white silk upper garment, with a fine umbrella and the best of fly-whisks, his body adorned with cosmetics, resplendent, his limbs illumined by the radiance of ornamental gems — like the full moon amid the stars. (Verse 3)

body.text:
tataḥ praviśati yathānirdiṣṭo duryodhanaḥ| duryodhanaḥ uddhūtaroṣamiva me
hṛdayaṃ saharṣaṃ prāptaṃ
raṇotsavamimaṃ sahasā vicintya| icchāmi pāṇḍavabale varavāraṇānā-
mutkṛttadantamusalāni
mukhāni kartum|| 4|| kāñcukīyaḥ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Duryodhana</s> enters as described. <s>Duryodhana</s>: My heart, with anger aroused, together with joy, contemplating this sudden festival of battle — I wish to make the faces of the best war-elephants in the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army into mortars with their tusks cut off! (Verse 4) Chamberlain:
Victory to the great king! By the great king's command, the entire assembly of kings has been brought together.
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Well done. You — enter the inner apartments.
Chamberlain:
As the great king commands.
He exits. <s>Duryodhana</s>:

body.text:
āryau vaikarṇavarṣadevau ucyatām| asti mamaikādaśākṣauhiṇībalasamudayaḥ| asya
kaḥ
senāpatirbhavitumarhatīti| kimāhaturbhavantau| mahānkhalvayamarthaḥ|
mantrayitvā vaktavyamiti|
sadṛśametat| tadāgamyatāṃ mantraśālāmeva praviśāmaḥ|
body.translated_text: Noble <s>Vikarṇa</s> and <s>Varṣadeva</s>, let it be said: I have a force of eleven <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s> (army divisions). Who is worthy to be the commander-in-chief of this force? What say you, sirs? This is indeed a great matter. It should be discussed and then spoken. That is fitting. Then let us proceed — let us enter the council hall itself.

body.text:
ācārya abhivādaye| praviśatu bhavānmantraśālām| pitāmaha abhivādaye| praviśatu
bhavānmantraśālām| mātula abhivādaye| praviśatu bhavānmantraśālām| āryau
vaikarṇavarṣadevau praviśatāṃ bhavantau| bho bhoḥ sarvakṣatriyāḥ svairaṃ
praviśantu bhavantaḥ|
vayasya karṇa praviśāvastāvat|
body.translated_text: Teacher, I salute you — please enter the council hall. Grandsire, I salute you — please enter the council hall. Uncle, I salute you — please enter the council hall. Noble <s>Vikarṇa</s> and <s>Varṣadeva</s> — please enter, sirs. Ho, all <s>kṣatriyas</s> (warriors) — please enter at your leisure, sirs. Friend <s>Karṇa</s>, let us enter now.

body.text:
praviśya|ācārya etatkūrmāsanam| āsyatām| pitāmaha etatsiṃhāsanam| āsyatām| mātula
etaccarmāsanam| āsyatām| āryau vaikarṇavarṣadevau āsātāṃ bhavantau| bho bhoḥ
sarvakṣatriyāḥ
svairamāsatāṃ bhavantaḥ| kimiti kimiti| mahārājo nāsta iti| aho sevādharmaḥ|
nanvayamahamāse|
vayasya karṇa tvamapyāssva|
body.translated_text: (Having entered) Teacher, this is the tortoise-seat — please be seated. Grandsire, this is the lion-throne — please be seated. Uncle, this is the leather seat — please be seated. Noble <s>Vikarṇa</s> and <s>Varṣadeva</s> — please be seated, sirs. Ho, all <s>kṣatriyas</s> — please be seated at your leisure, sirs. What is this? What is this? 'The great king does not sit' — say they. Ah, the duty of service! But here am I — I sit. Friend <s>Karṇa</s>, you too sit down.

body.text:
upaviśya|āryau vaikarṇavarṣadevau ucyatām| asti
mamaikādaśākṣauhiṇībalasamudayaḥ| asya kaḥ
senāpatirbhavitumarhatīti|
body.translated_text: (Having sat down) Noble <s>Vikarṇa</s> and <s>Varṣadeva</s>, let it be said: I have a force of eleven <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s>. Who is worthy to be the commander-in-chief of this force?
What say you, sirs? 'The honorable king of <s>Gāndhāra</s> will speak on this,' you say? Very well, let it be stated by the uncle.

body.text:
kimāha mātulaḥ| atrabhavati gāṅgeye sthite ko.anyaḥ senāpatirbhavitumarhatīti|
samyagāha mātulaḥ|
bhavatu bhavatu pitāmaha eva bhavatu| vayamapyetadabhilaṣāmaḥ|
body.translated_text: What does the uncle say? 'While the honorable <s>Gāṅgeya</s> (Bhīṣma) stands here, who else is worthy to be commander-in-chief?' The uncle speaks rightly. Very well, very well — let the grandsire himself be [the commander]. We too desire exactly this.

body.text:
senāninādapaṭahasvanaśaṅkhanādai- ścaṇḍānilāhatamahodadhinādakalpaiḥ|
gāṅgeyamūrdhni
patitairabhiṣekatoyaiḥ sārdhaṃ patantu hṛdayāni narādhipānām|| 5|| praviśya|
kāñcukīyaḥ
body.translated_text: With the sounds of the commander's drums, conch-shells, and kettledrums, resembling the roar of the great ocean struck by fierce winds, let the hearts of kings fall together with the consecration waters poured upon the head of <s>Gāṅgeya</s>! (Verse 5) (Entering) Chamberlain:

body.text:
jayatu mahārājaḥ| eṣa khalu pāṇḍavaskandhāvārāddautyenāgataḥ puruṣottamo
nārāyaṇaḥ|
body.translated_text: Victory to the great king! This <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person), <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, has come as an envoy from the camp of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.
<s>Duryodhana</s>:

body.text:
mā tāvat| bho bādarāyaṇa kiṃ kiṃ kaṃsabhṛtyo dāmodarastava puruṣottamaḥ| sa
gopālakastava
puruṣottamaḥ| bārhadrathāpahṛtaviṣayakīrtibhogastava puruṣottamaḥ| aho
pārthivāsannamāśritya
bhṛtyajanasya samudācāraḥ| sagarvaṃ khalvasya vacanam| ā apadhvaṃsa|
body.translated_text: Stop there! Ho, <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> — what! Is <s>Dāmodara</s>, the servant of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, your 'Supreme Person'? Is that cowherd your 'Supreme Person'? Is he whose dominion, fame, and enjoyments were stolen by the son of <s>Bṛhadratha</s> your 'Supreme Person'? Ah, the behavior of servants when they are close to kings! His words are indeed arrogant! Away with you, begone!
Chamberlain:

body.text: prasīdatu mahārājaḥ| saṃbhrameṇa samudācāro vismṛtaḥ|pādayoḥ patati|
body.translated_text: May the great king be gracious! In my confusion, I forgot the proper protocol. (He falls at his feet.)
<s>Duryodhana</s>:

body.text: saṃbhrama iti| ā manuṣyāṇāmastyeva saṃbhramaḥ| uttiṣṭhotiṣṭha|
body.translated_text: 'Confusion,' he says! Well, men do indeed have confusion. Get up, get up.
Chamberlain:
I am favored.
<s>Duryodhana</s>:

body.text: idānīṃ prasanno.asmi| ka eṣa dūtaḥ prāptaḥ|
body.translated_text: Now I am appeased. Who is this envoy that has arrived?
Chamberlain:
The envoy who has arrived is <s>Keśava</s>.
<s>Duryodhana</s>:

body.text:
keśava iti| evameṣṭavyam| ayameva samudācāraḥ| bho bho rājānaḥ dautyenāgatasya
keśavasya kiṃ
yuktam|
body.translated_text: '<s>Keśava</s>' — thus it should be said. This is the proper protocol. Ho there, kings! What is proper for <s>Keśava</s>, who has come as an envoy?

body.text:
kimāhurbhavantaḥ| arghyapradānena pūjayitavyaḥ keśava iti| na me rocate|
grahaṇamasyātra hitaṃ
paśyāmi|
body.translated_text: What say you, sirs? '<s>Keśava</s> should be honored with the offering of the welcome gift (<s>arghya</s>),' you say? That does not please me. I see his arrest as advantageous here.

body.text:
grahaṇamupagate tu vāsubhadre hṛtanayanā iva pāṇḍavā bhaveyuḥ| gatimatirahiteṣu
pāṇḍaveṣu
kṣitirakhilāpi bhavenmamāsapatnā|| 6||
body.translated_text: If <s>Vāsubhadra</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) were arrested, the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, as if robbed of their eyes, would be rendered helpless. With the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> bereft of guidance and counsel, the entire earth would become mine without a rival. (Verse 6)

body.text:
api ca yo.atra keśavasya pratyutthāsyati sa mayā dvādaśasuvarṇabhāreṇa daṇḍyaḥ|
tadapramattā
bhavantu bhavantaḥ|ātmagatam|ko nu khalvidānīṃ mamāpratyutthānasyopāyaḥ| hanta
dṛṣṭa
upāyaḥ|prakāśam|bādarāyaṇa ānīyatāṃ sa citrapaṭo nanu yatra
draupadīkeśāmbarāvakarṣaṇamālikhitam|ātmagatam|tasmindṛṣṭivinyāsaṃ
kurvannotthāsyāmi
keśavasya|
body.translated_text: Moreover, whoever stands up to receive <s>Keśava</s> shall be fined twelve gold <s>bhāras</s> (measures) by me. So be alert, sirs! (Aside) Now then, what stratagem can I devise for not standing up? Aha, I have found a stratagem! (Aloud) <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, bring that painted scroll — the one on which the disrobing and hair-dragging of <s>Draupadī</s> is depicted. (Aside) By fixing my gaze upon it, I shall not stand up for <s>Keśava</s>.
Chamberlain:

body.text: yadājñāpayati mahārājaḥ|niṣkramya praviśya|jayatu mahārājaḥ| ayaṃ sa citrapaṭaḥ|
body.translated_text: As the great king commands. (Exits and re-enters) Victory to the great king! Here is that painted scroll.
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Spread it out before me.
Chamberlain:
As the great king commands. (He spreads it out.)
<s>Duryodhana</s>:

body.text:
aho darśanīyo.ayaṃ citrapaṭaḥ| eṣa duḥśāsano draupadīṃ keśahaste gṛhītavān| eṣā
khalu
draupadī|
body.translated_text: Ah, what a sight this painted scroll is! Here is <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, who has seized <s>Draupadī</s> by the hair! And here indeed is <s>Draupadī</s> —
Seized by <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, with eyes wide open in alarm, she shines like a crescent moon caught within the jaws of <s>Rāhu</s>. (Verse 7)

body.text:
eṣa durātmā bhīmaḥ sarvarājasamakṣamavamānitāṃ draupadīṃ dṛṣṭvā
pravṛddhāmarṣaḥ
sabhāstambhaṃ tulayati| eṣa yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
body.translated_text: Here is the wicked <s>Bhīma</s> — seeing <s>Draupadī</s> humiliated before all the assembled kings, his fury swelling, he is shaking the pillar of the assembly hall! Here is <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> —
endowed with truth, <s>dharma</s>, and compassion, his mind confounded by the dice-game, with sidelong glances he calms the rage of <s>Vṛkodara</s> (Bhīma). (Verse 8)
Here now is <s>Arjuna</s> —

body.text:
roṣākulākṣaḥ sphuritādharoṣṭhastṛṇāya matvā ripumaṇḍalaṃ tat| utsādayiṣyanniva
sarvarājñaḥ
śanaiḥ samākarṣati gāṇḍivajyām|| 9||
body.translated_text: with eyes agitated by rage, his lower lip quivering, regarding that circle of enemies as mere straw, as if about to annihilate all the kings, he slowly draws the string of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> (his bow). (Verse 9)
Here is <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> restraining <s>Arjuna</s>. These two are <s>Nakula</s> and <s>Sahadeva</s> —

body.text:
kṛtaparikarabandhau carmanistriṃśahastau paruṣitamukharāgau
spaṣṭadaṣṭādharoṣṭhau|
vigatamaraṇaśaṅkau satvaraṃ bhrātaraṃ me harimiva mṛgapotau tejasābhiprayātau||
body.translated_text: with girdles fastened, shield and sword in hand, with faces flushed with anger, clearly biting their lower lips, heedless of death, swiftly advancing upon my brother with their might, like two young deer [advancing] upon a lion. (Verse 10)
Here is <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> approaching the two princes and restraining them.

body.text:
nīco.ahameva viparītamatiḥ kathaṃ vā roṣaṃ parityajatamadya nayānayajñau|
dyūtādhikāramavamānamamṛṣyamāṇāḥ sattvādhikeṣu vacanīyaparākramāḥ syuḥ|| 11||
body.translated_text: 'It is I who am base, of perverted mind — but why? Abandon your anger today, O you who know right from wrong! Unable to bear the humiliation of the gambling-bout, those whose valor is to be spoken of among the mighty should show restraint.' (Verse 11)
Thus [he speaks]. Here is the king of <s>Gāndhāra</s> —

body.text:
akṣānkṣipansa kitavaḥ prahasansagarvaṃ saṃkocayanniva mudaṃ dviṣatāṃ
svakīrtyā| svairāsano
drupadarājasutāṃ rudantīṃ kākṣeṇa paśyati likhatyapi gāṃ nayajñaḥ|| 12||
body.translated_text: That gambler, throwing the dice while laughing proudly, as if contracting the joy of his enemies with his own fame, seated at ease, looks sideways at the weeping daughter of King <s>Drupada</s>, and also marks the ground — he who knows statecraft. (Verse 12)

body.text:
etāvācāryapitāmahau tāṃ dṛṣṭvā lajjāyamānau paṭāntāntarhitamukhau sthitau| aho
asya
varṇāḍhyatā| aho bhāvopapannatā| aho yuktalekhatā| suvyaktamālikhito.ayaṃ
citrapaṭaḥ|
prīto.asmi| ko.atra|
body.translated_text: Here are the Teacher and the Grandsire — seeing her, overcome with shame, they stand with their faces hidden behind the edge of a cloth. Ah, the richness of its coloring! Ah, the aptness of expression! Ah, the skillfulness of the drawing! This painted scroll has been clearly depicted. I am pleased! Who is there?
Chamberlain:
Victory to the great king!
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, bring in that envoy, who is amazed merely at the sight of the bird-vehicle.
Chamberlain:
As the great king commands.
He exits. <s>Duryodhana</s>:

body.text:
vayasya karṇa
prāptaḥ kilādya vacanādiha pāṇḍavānāṃ dautyena bhṛtya iva kṛṣṇamatiḥ sa kṛṣṇaḥ|
śrotuṃ
sakhe tvamapi sajjaya karṇa karṇau nārīmṛdūni vacanāni yudhiṣṭhirasya|| 13|| tataḥ
praviśati
vāsudevaḥ kāñcukīyaśca| vāsudevaḥ
body.translated_text: Friend <s>Karṇa</s> — today, as an envoy conveying the words of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, of dark intelligence, has arrived here like a servant. Prepare your ears too, O friend <s>Karṇa</s>, to hear the soft, womanly words of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>! (Verse 13) Then <s>Vāsudeva</s> enters, together with the chamberlain. <s>Vāsudeva</s>:

body.text:
adya khalu dharmarājavacanāddhanaṃjayākṛtrimamitratayā
cāhavadarpamanuktagrāhiṇaṃ
suyodhanaṃ prati mayāpyanucitadautyasamayo.anuṣṭhitaḥ| atha ca
body.translated_text: Today indeed, at the command of <s>Dharmarāja</s> (Yudhiṣṭhira) and due to <s>Dhanañjaya</s>'s (Arjuna's) genuine friendship, the occasion of this unsuitable embassy has been undertaken by me toward <s>Suyodhana</s> (Duryodhana), who seizes upon the pride of battle without being asked. And further —

body.text:
kṛṣṇāparābhavabhuvā ripuvāhinībha- kumbhasthalīdalanatīkṣṇagadādharasya|
bhīmasya
kopaśikhinā yudhi pārthapattri- caṇḍānilaiśca kuruvaṃśavanaṃ vinaṣṭam|| 14||
body.translated_text: By the fire of <s>Bhīma</s>'s wrath — he who bears a mace sharp enough to split the frontal globes of enemy war-elephants, born from the humiliation of <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (Draupadī) — and by the fierce winds of <s>Pārtha</s>'s (Arjuna's) arrows in battle, the forest of the <s>Kuru</s> lineage is destroyed. // 14 //
This is <s>Suyodhana</s>'s camp. Here indeed —

body.text:
āvāsāḥ pārthivānāṃ surapurasadṛśāḥ svacchandavihitā vistīrṇāḥ śastraśālā
bahuvidhakaraṇaiḥ śastrairupacitāḥ| heṣante mandurāsthāsturagavaraghaṭā bṛṃhanti
kariṇa
aiśvaryaṃ sphītametatsvajanaparibhavādāsannavilayam|| 15||
body.translated_text: The quarters of the kings, resembling the city of the gods, spacious and freely arranged; the armories filled with weapons of many kinds; in the stables, herds of excellent horses neigh, and elephants trumpet. This immense sovereignty, though flourishing, is near destruction on account of the humiliation of one's own kinsmen. // 15 //
Ho!

body.text:
duṣṭavādī guṇadveṣī śaṭhaḥ svajananirdayaḥ| suyodhano hi māṃ dṛṣṭvā naiva
kāryaṃ kariṣyati||
body.translated_text: Wicked in speech, hostile to virtues, deceitful, merciless to his own people — <s>Suyodhana</s>, upon seeing me, will not accomplish the task at all.
Ho, <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, shall I enter?
Chamberlain:
What else, what else! <s>Padmanābha</s> may enter.
<s>Vāsudeva</s>:

body.text:
praviśya| kathaṃ kathaṃ māṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃbhrāntāḥ sarvakṣatriyāḥ| alamalaṃ
saṃbhrameṇa|
svairamāsatāṃ bhavantaḥ|
body.translated_text: (Entering.) What! All the <s>kṣatriyas</s> are agitated upon seeing me! Enough, enough of this agitation! Let the honorable ones be seated at ease.
<s>Duryodhana</s>:

body.text:
kathaṃ kathaṃ keśavaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃbhrāntāḥ sarvakṣatriyāḥ| alamalaṃ saṃbhrameṇa|
smaraṇīyaḥ pūrvamāśrāvito daṇḍaḥ| nanvahamājñaptā|
body.translated_text: What! All the <s>kṣatriyas</s> are agitated upon seeing <s>Keśava</s>! Enough, enough of this agitation! Remember the punishment previously announced! Am I not the one who commands?
<s>Vāsudeva</s>:
(Approaching.) Ho, <s>Suyodhana</s>, why do you remain seated?
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
(Falling from his seat, aside:) Clearly, <s>Keśava</s> has indeed arrived.

body.text:
utsāhena matiṃ kṛtvāpyāsīno.asmi samāhitaḥ| keśavasya prabhāvena
calito.asmyāsanādaham|| 17||
body.translated_text: Though I had resolved with effort to remain seated and composed, by the power of <s>Keśava</s> I was dislodged from my seat. // 17 //
Ah, this envoy is very crafty! (Aloud:) Ho, envoy, be seated on this seat.
<s>Vāsudeva</s>:

body.text:
ācārya āsyatāṃ| gāṅgeyapramukhā rājānaḥ svairamāsatāṃ bhavantaḥ|
vayamapyupaviśāmaḥ|upaviśya|aho darśanīyo.ayaṃ citrapaṭaḥ| mā tāvat|
draupadīkeśāmbarākarṣaṇamatrālikhitam| aho nu khalu
body.translated_text: Let the Teacher (<s>Droṇa</s>) be seated. Let the kings led by <s>Gāṅgeya</s> (Bhīṣma) be seated at ease. We too shall sit down. (Sitting down.) Ah, what a sight this painted scroll is! But wait — the hair-dragging and garment-pulling of <s>Draupadī</s> is depicted here! Ah, indeed —

body.text:
suyodhano.ayaṃ svajanāvamānaṃ parākramaṃ paśyati bāliśatvāt| ko nāma loke
svayamātmadoṣamudghāṭayennaṣṭaghṛṇaḥ sabhāsu|| 18||
body.translated_text: This <s>Suyodhana</s>, in his foolishness, regards the humiliation of his own kinsmen as valor. Who indeed in the world, devoid of all shame, would openly display his own fault in the assembly? // 18 //
Ah! Let this painted scroll be removed!
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, the painted scroll is to be removed, it seems!
Chamberlain:
As the great king commands. (He removes it.)
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Ho, envoy —

body.text:
dharmātmajo vāyusutaśca bhīmo bhrātārjuno me tridaśendrasūnuḥ| yamau ca
tāvaśvisutau vinītau
sarve sabhṛtyāḥ kuśalopapannāḥ|| 19|| vāsudevaḥ
body.translated_text: Is <s>Dharmarāja</s> (the son of <s>Dharma</s>) well? And <s>Bhīma</s>, the son of the Wind? And my kinsman <s>Arjuna</s>, the son of the lord of the thirty gods? And the well-mannered twins, the sons of the <s>Aśvins</s>? Are all of them with their servants in good health? // 19 // <s>Vāsudeva</s>:

body.text:
sadṛśametadgāndhārīputrasya| atha kimatha kim| kuśalinaḥ sarve| bhavato rājye
śarīre
bāhyābhyantare ca kuśalamanāmayaṃ ca pṛṣṭvā vijñāpayanti yudhiṣṭhirādayaḥ
pāṇḍavāḥ|
body.translated_text: This is fitting for the son of <s>Gāndhārī</s>. What else, what else? All are well. Having inquired about the welfare and health of your kingdom, your person, and both external and internal affairs, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> and the other <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> inform you:

body.text:
anubhūtaṃ mahadduḥkhaṃ saṃpūrṇaḥ samayaḥ sa ca| asmākamapi dharmyaṃ
yaddāyādyaṃ
tadvibhajyatām|| 20||
body.translated_text: 'Great suffering has been endured, and that covenant is now fulfilled. Let that inheritance which is rightfully ours also be divided.' // 20 //
Thus.
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
What, what — 'inheritance,' you say? Ho!

body.text:
vane pitṛvyo mṛgayāprasaṃgataḥ kṛtāparādho muniśāpamāptavān| tadāprabhṛtyeva sa
dāraniḥspṛhaḥ parātmajānāṃ pitṛtāṃ kathaṃ vrajet|| 21|| vāsudevaḥ
body.translated_text: 'The uncle (<s>Pāṇḍu</s>), while hunting in the forest, committed an offense and received a sage's curse. From that time onward he was indifferent to women. How then could he be the father of others' sons?' // 21 // <s>Vāsudeva</s>:
I do not ask you about old times.

body.text:
vicitravīryo viṣayī vipattiṃ kṣayeṇa yātaḥ punarambikāyām| vyāsena jāto
dhṛtarāṣṭra eva labheta
rājyaṃ janakaḥ kathaṃ te|| 22||
body.translated_text: <s>Vicitravīrya</s>, a sensualist, perished by consumption. Then <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> was begotten by <s>Vyāsa</s> upon <s>Ambikā</s>. How then should your father obtain the kingdom? // 22 //
No, no, sir!

body.text:
evaṃ parasparavirodhavivardhanena śīghraṃ bhavetkurukulaṃ nṛpa nāmaśeṣam|
tatkartumarhati
bhavānapakṛtya roṣaṃ yattvāṃ yudhiṣṭhiramukhāḥ praṇayādbruvanti|| 23||
body.translated_text: By this mutual escalation of hostility, O king, the <s>Kuru</s> family will quickly become merely a name. Therefore, please set aside your anger and do what those led by <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> say to you in affection. // 23 //
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Ho, envoy, you do not understand the ways of royal governance.

body.text:
rājyaṃ nāma nṛpātmajaiḥ sahṛdairjitvā ripūnbhujyate talloke na tu yācyate na tu
punardīnāya vā
dīyate| kāṅkṣā cennṛpatitvamāptumacirātkurvantu te sāhasaṃ svairaṃ vā praviśantu
śāntamatibhirjuṣṭaṃ śamāyāśramam|| 24|| vāsudevaḥ
body.translated_text: A kingdom is enjoyed by princes and their allies after conquering enemies; it is not begged for in the world, nor is it given to the destitute. If they desire to obtain kingship, let them soon commit an act of daring, or else let them freely enter the hermitage favored by those of tranquil minds, for the sake of peace. // 24 // <s>Vāsudeva</s>:
Ho, <s>Suyodhana</s>, enough of speaking harshly to one's kinsmen.

body.text:
puṇyasaṃcayaprāptāmadhigamya nṛpaśriyam| vañcayedyaḥ suhṛdbandhūnsa
bhavedviphalaśramaḥ|| 25|| duryodhanaḥ
body.translated_text: He who, having attained royal fortune acquired through the accumulation of merit, would cheat his friends and relatives — his efforts would be in vain. // 25 // <s>Duryodhana</s>:
Ho, envoy —

body.text:
syālaṃ tava gurorbhūpaṃ kaṃsaṃ na te dayā| kathamasmākamevaṃ syātteṣu
nityāpakāriṣu|| 26||
body.translated_text: You had no compassion for <s>Kaṃsa</s>, your own guru's father-in-law, a king. How then would we have such compassion toward those who constantly harm us? // 26 //
<s>Vāsudeva</s>:

body.text:
alaṃ tanmaddoṣato jñātum|
kṛtvā putraviyogārtāṃ bahuśo jananīṃ mama| vṛddhaṃ svapitaraṃ baddhvā hato.ayaṃ
mṛtyunā
svayam|| 27|| duryodhanaḥ
body.translated_text: Enough of attributing that as my fault. Having many times caused my mother grief through the separation from her sons, having imprisoned my aged father — he was slain by death itself. // 27 // <s>Duryodhana</s>:

body.text: sarvathā vañcitastvayā kaṃsaḥ| alamātmastavena| na śauryametat| paśya|
body.translated_text: In every way, <s>Kaṃsa</s> was deceived by you! Enough of self-praise! That is not valor! Look —

body.text:
jāmātṛnāśavyasanābhitapte roṣābhibhūte magadheśvare.atha| palāyamānasya
bhayāturasya
śauryaṃ tadetatkva gataṃ tavāsīt|| 28|| vāsudevaḥ
body.translated_text: When the lord of <s>Magadha</s> (<s>Jarāsandha</s>), tormented by the grief of his sons-in-law's destruction, was overcome with fury — where had that valor of yours gone, as you fled in terror? // 28 // <s>Vāsudeva</s>:

body.text:
bhoḥ suyodhana deśakālāvasthāpekṣitaṃ khalu śauryaṃ nayānugāminām| iha
tiṣṭhatu
tāvadasmadgataḥ parihāsaḥ| svakāryamanuṣṭhīyatām|
body.translated_text: Ho, <s>Suyodhana</s>, for those who follow wise policy, valor depends on place, time, and circumstance. Let the ridicule directed at us be set aside for now. Let your own business be attended to.

body.text:
kartavyo bhrātṛṣu sneho vismartavyā guṇetarāḥ| saṃbandho bandhubhiḥ
śreyānlokayorubhayorapi||
body.translated_text: Affection should be maintained toward brothers; faults should be forgotten. The bond with kinsmen is auspicious for both worlds.

body.text:
29|| duryodhanaḥ devātmajairmanuṣyāṇāṃ kathaṃ vā bandhutā bhavet|
piṣṭapeṣaṇametāvatparyāptaṃ chidyatāṃ kathā|| 30|| vāsudevaḥ
body.translated_text: // 29 // <s>Duryodhana</s>: How can there be kinship between sons of gods and mortals? This is but grinding what is already ground flour. Enough — let the conversation be cut short. // 30 // <s>Vāsudeva</s>:
(Aside:)

body.text:
prasādyamānaḥ sāmnāyaṃ na svabhāvaṃ vimuñcati| hanta saṃkṣobhayāmyenaṃ
vacobhiḥ
paruṣākṣaraiḥ|| 31||
body.translated_text: Though being conciliated with gentle words, this one does not abandon his nature. Well then, I shall provoke him with words of harsh syllables. // 31 //

body.text: prakāśam|bhoḥ suyodhana kiṃ na jānīṣe.arjunasya balaparākramam|
body.translated_text: (Aloud:) Ho, <s>Suyodhana</s>, do you not know the strength and valor of <s>Arjuna</s>?
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
I do not know.
<s>Vāsudeva</s>:
Ho, listen then!

body.text:
kairātaṃ vapurāsthitaḥ paśupatiryuddhena saṃtoṣito vahneḥ khāṇḍavamaśnataḥ
sumahatī vṛṣṭiḥ
śaraiśchāditā| devendrārtikarā nivātakavacā nītāḥ kṣayaṃ līlayā nanvekena tadā
virāṭanagare
bhīṣmādayo nirjitāḥ|| 32||
body.translated_text: <s>Paśupati</s> (Śiva), having assumed the form of a <s>Kirāta</s> (hunter), was pleased by <s>Arjuna</s> in combat. The mighty rain of <s>Indra</s>, as <s>Agni</s> consumed the <s>Khāṇḍava</s> forest, was blocked by his arrows. The <s>Nivātakavacas</s>, who caused <s>Indra</s> distress, were destroyed with ease. Was it not by him alone that <s>Bhīṣma</s> and the others were defeated at the city of <s>Virāṭa</s>? // 32 //
Moreover, I shall tell you another thing that was before your very own eyes.

body.text:
nanu tvaṃ citrasenena nīyamāno nabhastalam| vikrośanghoṣayātrāyāṃ phalgunenaiva
mokṣitaḥ|| 33||
body.translated_text: Were you not, when being carried off to the sky by <s>Citrasena</s> (the <s>Gandharva</s>), crying aloud during the festive procession, freed by <s>Phalguna</s> (Arjuna) himself? // 33 //
What more need be said?

body.text:
dātumarhasi madvākyādrājyārdhaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraja| anyathā sāgarāntāṃ gāṃ hariṣyanti
hi
pāṇḍavāḥ|| 34|| duryodhanaḥ
body.translated_text: You should give half the kingdom at my word, O son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>. Otherwise the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> will seize the earth up to the oceans. // 34 // <s>Duryodhana</s>:
What, what? 'The <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> will seize,' you say?

body.text:
praharati yadi yuddhe māruto bhīmarūpī praharati yadi sākṣātpārtharūpeṇa śakraḥ|
paruṣavacanadakṣa tvadvacobhirna dāsye tṛṇamapi pitṛbhukte vīryagupte svarājye||
body.translated_text: Even if the Wind-god in <s>Bhīma</s>'s form strikes in battle, even if <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) himself strikes in <s>Pārtha</s>'s (Arjuna's) form — O you skilled in harsh speech, by your words I shall not give even a blade of grass of this ancestral kingdom guarded by valor.
// 35 // <s>Vāsudeva</s>:

body.text: bhoḥ kurukulakalaṅkabhūta ayaśolubdha vayaṃ kila tṛṇāntarābhibhāṣakāḥ|
body.translated_text: Ho, you who are a stain upon the <s>Kuru</s> family, greedy for infamy — are we then speakers from behind blades of grass?
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Ho, cowherd — it is blades of grass that you are fit to address!

body.text:
avadhyāṃ pramadāṃ hatvā hayaṃ govṛṣameva ca| mallānapi sunirlajjo vaktumicchasi
sādhubhiḥ||
body.translated_text: Having killed a defenseless woman, a horse, a cow-bull, and wrestlers too — utterly shameless, you still wish to speak among the noble? // 36 //
// 36 // <s>Vāsudeva</s>:
Ho, <s>Suyodhana</s>, do you indeed insult me?
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Is this not the truth?
<s>Vāsudeva</s>:
I shall leave then.
<s>Duryodhana</s>:

body.text: gaccha gaccha paśukhuroddhatareṇurūpitāṅgo vrajameva| viphalīkṛtaḥ kālaḥ|
body.translated_text: Go, go! Your body marked by dust raised by the hooves of cattle — go back to the cowherd settlement! Time has been wasted.
<s>Vāsudeva</s>:

body.text:
evamastu| na vayamanuktasaṃdeśā gantumicchāmaḥ| tadākarṇyatāṃ yudhiṣṭhirasya
saṃdeśaḥ|
body.translated_text: So be it. But we do not wish to depart without delivering the message. Therefore hear the message of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>.
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Bah! You are not to be spoken to!

body.text:
ahamavadhṛtapāṇḍarātapatro dvijavarahastadhṛtāmbusiktamūrdhā|
avanatanṛpamaṇḍalānuyātraiḥ
saha kathayāmi bhavadvidhairna bhāṣe|| 37|| vāsudevaḥ
body.translated_text: I, beneath my white parasol, with head anointed by water from the hands of the best of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, accompanied by processions of bowing kings — I converse with them. I do not speak with the likes of you. // 37 // <s>Vāsudeva</s>:

body.text: na vyāharati kila māṃ suyodhanaḥ| bhoḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Suyodhana</s> will not speak to me, it seems. Ho!
Rogue, devoid of affection for kinsmen, crow, squinting, tawny-eyed — for your sake this <s>Kuru</s> lineage will soon come to destruction! // 38 //
Ho, ho, kings — I shall take my leave now.
<s>Duryodhana</s>:

body.text:
kathaṃ yāsyati kila keśavaḥ| duḥśāsana durmarṣaṇa durmukha durbuddhe
duṣṭeśvara
dūtasamudācāramatikrāntaḥ keśavo badhyatām| kathamaśaktāḥ| duḥśāsana na
samarthaḥ
khalvasi|
body.translated_text: What, <s>Keśava</s> will leave, you say? <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, <s>Durmarṣaṇa</s>, <s>Durmukha</s>, <s>Durbuddhi</s>, <s>Duṣṭeśvara</s> — <s>Keśava</s> has violated the protocol of an envoy — let him be bound! What, are you unable? <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, are you not capable?

body.text:
karituraganihantā kaṃsahantā sa kṛṣṇaḥ paśupakulanivāsādānujīvyānabhijñaḥ|
hṛtabhujabalavīryaḥ pārthivānāṃ samakṣaṃ svavacanakṛtadoṣo badhyatāmeṣa
śīghram|| 39||
body.translated_text: That <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, slayer of elephants and horses, slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s> — unfamiliar with noble conduct, having lived among a cowherd community — his arms' strength and valor are now spent. Before the eyes of the kings, guilty by his own words, let him be bound quickly! // 39 //

body.text:
ayamaśaktaḥ| mātula badhyatāmayaṃ keśavaḥ| kathaṃ parāṅmukhaḥ patati| bhavatu|
ahameva
pāśairbadhnāmi|pāśamudyamyopasarpati|
body.translated_text: This one is incapable! Uncle, let this <s>Keśava</s> be bound! Why does he turn away and fall? So be it! I myself shall bind him with ropes! (Raising the ropes, he approaches.)
<s>Vāsudeva</s>:

body.text:
kathaṃ baddhukāmo māṃ kila suyodhanaḥ| bhavatu| suyodhanasya sāmarthyaṃ
paśyāmi|viśvarūpamāsthitaḥ|
body.translated_text: What! <s>Suyodhana</s> wishes to bind me! So be it! Let me see <s>Suyodhana</s>'s capability. (He assumes the cosmic form.)
<s>Duryodhana</s>:
Ho, envoy!

body.text:
sṛjasi yadi samantāddevamāyāḥ svamāyāḥ praharasi yadi vā tvaṃ durnivāraiḥ
surāstraiḥ|
hayagajavṛṣabhāṇāṃ pātanājjātadarpo narapatigaṇamadhye badhyase tvaṃ mayādya||
body.translated_text: Whether you deploy all around the divine illusions, your own illusions, or whether you strike with irresistible divine weapons — drunk with pride from felling horses, elephants, and bulls, you shall be bound by me today in the midst of this assembly of kings! (Verse 40)

body.text:
āḥ tiṣṭhedānīm| kathaṃ na dṛṣṭaḥ keśavaḥ| ayaṃ keśavaḥ| aho hrasvatvaṃ keśavasya|
āḥ
tiṣṭhedānīm| kathaṃ na dṛṣṭaḥ keśavaḥ| ayaṃ keśavaḥ| aho dīrghatvaṃ keśavasya|
kathaṃ na
dṛṣṭaḥ keśavaḥ| ayaṃ keśavaḥ| sarvatra mantraśālāyāṃ keśavā bhavanti| kimidānīṃ
kariṣye|
bhavatu dṛṣṭam| bho bho rājānaḥ ekenaikaḥ keśavo badhyatām| kathaṃ svayameva
pāśairbaddhāḥ
patanti rājānaḥ| sādhu bho jambhaka sādhu|
body.translated_text: Ah, stop now! What — <s>Keśava</s> is not seen! There is <s>Keśava</s>! Ah, how small <s>Keśava</s> has become! Ah, stop now! What — <s>Keśava</s> is not seen! There is <s>Keśava</s>! Ah, how tall <s>Keśava</s> has become! What — <s>Keśava</s> is not seen! There is <s>Keśava</s>! Everywhere in the council hall there are <s>Keśava</s>s! What shall I do now? So be it — I see! Ho ho, kings — let each one bind one <s>Keśava</s>! What — the kings themselves fall bound by ropes! Well done, O trickster, well done!

body.text:
matkārmukodaraviniḥsṛtabāṇajālai- rviddhaṃ kṣaratkṣatajarañjitasarvagātram|
paśyantu
pāṇḍutanayāḥ śibiropanītaṃ tvāṃ bāṣparuddhanayanāḥ pariniśvasantaḥ|| 41||
body.translated_text: Let the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> see you brought to the camp, your entire body wounded and drenched with blood flowing from your wounds, pierced by the shower of arrows released from the belly of my bow, while they choke with tears in their eyes and sigh deeply! (Verse 41)
Exit. <s>Vāsudeva</s>:

body.text: bhavatu pāṇḍavānāṃ kāryamahameva sādhayāmi| bhoḥ sudarśana itastāvat|
body.translated_text: So be it — I myself shall accomplish the task of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>. Ho, <s>Sudarśana</s>! Come hither!
Then <s>Sudarśana</s> enters. <s>Sudarśana</s>:
Here I am, sir!

body.text:
śrutvā giraṃ bhagavato vipulaprasādā- nnirdhāvito.asmi parivāritatoyadaughaḥ|
kasminkhalu
prakupitaḥ kamalāyatākṣaḥ kasyādya mūrdhani mayā pravijṛmbhitavyam|| 42||
body.translated_text: Having heard the word of the Lord, from his vast grace, I have rushed forth, surrounded by masses of clouds. At whom indeed is the lotus-eyed one angered? Upon whose head must I display my fury today? (Verse 42)
Where indeed is Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>?
He of unmanifest origin and inconceivable self, devoted to the protection of the worlds, one yet of many forms, the illustrious destroyer of enemy forces. (Verse 43)

body.text:
vilokya|aye ayaṃ bhagavānhastinapuradvāre dūtasamudācāreṇopasthitaḥ| kutaḥ
khalvāpaḥ kutaḥ
khalvāpaḥ| bhagavati ākāśagaṅge āpastāvat| hanta sravati|ācamyopasṛtya|jayatu
bhagavānnārāyaṇaḥ|praṇamati|
body.translated_text: (Looking) Ah, here the Lord has presented himself at the gate of <s>Hastināpura</s> on the occasion of an embassy! From where shall I find water? From where shall I find water? O heavenly <s>Gaṅgā</s>, water please! Ah, it flows! (Having sipped water ritually and approaching) Victory to Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>! (He bows.)
<s>Vāsudeva</s>:
<s>Sudarśana</s>, be of irresistible valor!
<s>Sudarśana</s>:
I am favored!
<s>Vāsudeva</s>:
Fortunately you have arrived at the time for action!
<s>Sudarśana</s>:

body.text: kathaṃ kathaṃ karmakāla iti| ājñāpayatu bhagavānājñāpayatu|
body.translated_text: What! What! 'The time for action,' you say? Let the Lord command! Let the Lord command!

body.text:
kiṃ merumandarakulaṃ parivartayāmi saṃkṣobhayāmi sakalaṃ makarālayaṃ vā|
nakṣatravaṃśamakhilaṃ bhuvi pātayāmi nāśakyamasti mama deva tava prasādāt|| 44||
body.translated_text: Shall I overturn the family of <s>Meru</s> and <s>Mandara</s> mountains? Or shall I agitate the entire abode of sea-creatures? Shall I bring down the entire host of stars upon the earth? Nothing is impossible for me, O Lord, by your grace! (Verse 44)
<s>Vāsudeva</s>:
Ho, <s>Sudarśana</s>, come hither! Ho, <s>Suyodhana</s>!

body.text:
yadi lavaṇajalaṃ vā kandaraṃ vā girīṇāṃ grahagaṇacaritaṃ vā vāyumārgaṃ prayāsi|
mama
bhujabalayogaprāptasaṃjātavegaṃ bhavatu capala cakraṃ kālacakraṃ tavādya|| 45||
body.translated_text: Whether you flee to the salt ocean, or to the caverns of mountains, or to the sky-path traversed by planets — let my discus, having gained speed through the power of my arms, become the wheel of death for you today, O restless one! (Verse 45)
<s>Sudarśana</s>:
Ho, wretch <s>Suyodhana</s>, stop, stop! (Reconsidering) May Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> be gracious!

body.text:
mahībhārāpanayanaṃ kartuṃ jātasya bhūtale| asminnevaṃ gate deva nanu
syādviphalaśramaḥ|| 46||
body.translated_text: If you, who were born on earth to remove the burden of the earth, should act thus, O Lord, would it not then be effort in vain? (Verse 46)
<s>Vāsudeva</s>:
<s>Sudarśana</s>, in my anger proper conduct was not observed. Return to your own abode.
<s>Sudarśana</s>:

body.text:
yadājñāpayati bhagavānnārāyaṇaḥ| kathaṃ kathaṃ gopālaka iti| tricaraṇātikrāntatriloko
nārāyaṇaḥ khalvatra bhagavān| śaraṇaṃ vrajantu bhavantaḥ| yāvadgacchāmi| aye
etadbhagavadāyudhavaraṃ śārṅgaṃ prāptam|
body.translated_text: As Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> commands. What! What! 'Cowherd,' you say? Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who with three strides crossed over the three worlds, is indeed here! Take refuge, all of you! Now I shall go. Ah, here comes the excellent weapon of the Lord — the bow <s>Śārṅga</s>!

body.text:
tanumṛdulalitāṅgaṃ strīsvabhāvopapannaṃ harikaradhṛtamadhyaṃ
śatrusaṃghaikakālaḥ|
kanakakhacitapṛṣṭhaṃ bhāti kṛṣṇasya pārśve navasaliladapārśve cāruvidyullekheva||
body.translated_text: Slender, soft, and graceful of limb, endowed with a woman's nature, grasped at the middle by <s>Hari</s>'s hand, the single death-moment for hosts of enemies, with a gold-inlaid back — it shines beside <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> like a beautiful streak of lightning beside a fresh rain-cloud.

body.text:
bho bhoḥ śārṅga praśāntaroṣo bhagavānnārāyaṇaḥ| gamyatāṃ svanilayameva| hanta
nivṛttaḥ|
yāvadgacchāmi| aye iyaṃ kaumodakī prāptā|
body.translated_text: Ho ho, <s>Śārṅga</s>! Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s anger is appeased. Return to your own abode. Ah, it has turned back! Now I shall go. Ah, here comes the mace <s>Kaumodakī</s>!

body.text:
maṇikanakavicitrā citramālottarīyā suraripugaṇagātradhvaṃsane jātatṛṣṇā|
girivarataṭarūpā
durnivārātivīryā vrajati nabhasi śīghraṃ meghavṛndānuyātrā|| 48||
body.translated_text: Adorned with gems and gold, wearing a garland of variegated flowers as an upper garment, thirsting for the destruction of the bodies of hosts of enemies of the gods, resembling the slope of the best of mountains, of irresistible valor — she moves swiftly through the sky, accompanied by a retinue of clouds. (Verse 48)

body.text:
he kaumodaki praśāntaroṣo bhagavānnārāyaṇaḥ| hanta nivṛttā| yāvadgacchāmi| aye
ayaṃ
pāñcajanyaḥ prāptaḥ|
body.translated_text: Ho, <s>Kaumodakī</s>! Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s anger is appeased. Ah, she has turned back! Now I shall go. Ah, here comes the conch <s>Pāñcajanya</s>!

body.text:
pūrṇendukundakumudodarahāragauro nārāyaṇānanasarojakṛtaprasādaḥ| yasya svanaṃ
pralayasāgaraghoṣatulyaṃ garbhā niśamya nipatantyasurāṅganānām|| 49||
body.translated_text: White as the full moon, jasmine, white lily, the interior of a pearl necklace — graced by the lotus-face of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, hearing whose sound, equal to the roar of the ocean at the dissolution of the world, the fetuses of demonesses fall. (Verse 49)

body.text:
he pāñcajanya praśāntaroṣo bhagavān| gamyatāṃ svanilayameva| hanta nivṛttaḥ| aye
nandakāsiḥ
prāptaḥ|
body.translated_text: Ho, <s>Pāñcajanya</s>! The Lord's anger is appeased. Return to your own abode. Ah, it has turned back! Here comes the sword <s>Nandaka</s>!

body.text:
vanitāvigraho yuddhe mahāsurabhayaṃkaraḥ| prayāti gagane śīghraṃ maholkeva
vibhātyayam|| 50||
body.translated_text: Of womanly form, yet in battle terrifying to great <s>Asuras</s> (demons) — it moves swiftly through the sky and blazes like a great meteor. (Verse 50)

body.text:
he nandaka praśāntaroṣo bhagavān| gamyatāṃ svanilayameva| hanta nivṛttaḥ|
yāvadgacchāmi| aye
etāni bhagavadāyudhavarāṇi|
body.translated_text: Ho, <s>Nandaka</s>! The Lord's anger is appeased. Return to your own abode. Ah, it has turned back! Now I shall go. Ah, here are the excellent weapons of the Lord!

body.text:
so.ayaṃ khaḍgaḥ kharāṃśorapahasitatanuḥ svaiḥ karairnandakākhyaḥ seyaṃ
kaumodakī yā
suraripukaṭhinoraḥsthalakṣodadakṣā| saiṣā śārṅgābhidhānā pralayaghanaravajyāravā
cāpayaṣṭiḥ so.ayaṃ gambhīraghoṣaḥ śaśikaraviśadaḥ śaṅkharāṭpāñcajanyaḥ|| 51|| he
śārṅga kaumodaki pāñcajanya daityāntakṛnnandaka śatruvahne| praśāntaroṣo
bhagavānmurāriḥ
svasthānamevātra hi gaccha tāvat|| 52||
body.translated_text: Here is the sword named <s>Nandaka</s>, whose body outshines the fierce sun with its own rays; here is the mace <s>Kaumodakī</s>, skilled at shattering the hard chests of enemies of the gods; here is the bow-staff called <s>Śārṅga</s>, whose bowstring resounds like the thunder of clouds at the dissolution of the world; and here is that deep-sounding, moon-ray-white king of conches, <s>Pāñcajanya</s>! (Verse 51) Ho, <s>Śārṅga</s>! <s>Kaumodakī</s>! <s>Pāñcajanya</s>! <s>Nandaka</s>, destroyer of <s>Daityas</s>, fire against enemies! Lord <s>Murāri</s>'s anger is appeased — now go to your own abode! (Verse 52)

body.text:
hanta nivṛttāḥ| yāvadgacchāmi| aye atyuddhūto vāyuḥ| atitapatyādityaḥ| calitāḥ
parvatāḥ|
kṣubdhāḥ sāgarāḥ| patitā vṛkṣāḥ| bhrāntā meghāḥ| pralīnā vāsukiprabhṛtayo
bhujaṃgeśvarāḥ| kiṃ nu khalvidam| aye ayaṃ bhagavato vāhanaḥ garuḍaḥ prāptaḥ|
body.translated_text: Ah, they have turned back! Now I shall go. Ah, the wind has risen violently! The sun blazes excessively! The mountains tremble! The oceans are churning! Trees have fallen! Clouds are scattered! The serpent-kings led by <s>Vāsuki</s> have withdrawn! What indeed is this? Ah, here has come <s>Garuḍa</s>, the vehicle of the Lord!

body.text:
surāsurāṇāṃ parikhedalabdhaṃ yenāmṛtaṃ mātṛvimokṣaṇārthaṃ|
ācchinnamāsīddviṣato
murārestvāmudvahāmīti varo.api dattaḥ|| 53||
body.translated_text: By whom the <s>amṛta</s> (nectar of immortality), won through the toil of gods and demons, was seized from the enemy of <s>Murāri</s> for the purpose of freeing his mother — to him also was given the boon: 'I shall bear you.' (Verse 53)

body.text:
he kāśyapapriyasuta garuḍa praśāntaroṣo bhagavāndevadeveśaḥ| gamyatāṃ
svanilayameva| hanta
nivṛttaḥ| yāvadgacchāmi|
body.translated_text: Ho, dear son of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Garuḍa</s>! The Lord, the God of gods, is appeased in anger. Return to your own abode. Ah, he has turned back! Now I shall go.

body.text:
ete sthitā viyati kiṃnarayakṣasiddhāḥ devāśca saṃbhramacalanmukuṭottamāṅgāḥ|
ruṣṭe.acyute
vigatakāntiguṇāḥ praśāntaṃ śrutvā śrayanti sadanāni nivṛttatāpāḥ|| 54||
body.translated_text: These <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, and <s>Devas</s>, standing in the sky, their crowns trembling with agitation upon their heads — when <s>Acyuta</s> (the Unfallen One) was angered, they lost the quality of splendor; now, hearing that he is appeased, they return to their abodes, their distress removed. (Verse 54)
Now I too shall go to my lovely cave on Mount <s>Meru</s>.
Exit. <s>Vāsudeva</s>:
Now I too shall go to the camp of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.
Offstage:
No indeed, no indeed — you must not go!
<s>Vāsudeva</s>:

body.text: aye vṛddharājasvara iva| bho rājan eṣa sthito.asmi|
body.translated_text: Ah, it sounds like the voice of the aged king. O King, here I stand!
Then <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> enters. <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:

body.text:
kva nu khalu bhagavānnārāyaṇaḥ| kva nu khalu bhagavānpāṇḍavaśreyaskaraḥ| kva nu
khalu
bhagavānviprapriyaḥ| kva nu khalu bhagavāndevakīnandanaḥ|
body.translated_text: Where indeed is Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>? Where indeed is the Lord who seeks the welfare of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>? Where indeed is the Lord who is dear to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>? Where indeed is the Lord, the joy of <s>Devakī</s>?

body.text:
mama putrāparādhāttu śārṅgapāṇe tavādhunā| etanme tridaśādhyākṣa pādayoḥ
patitaṃ
śiraḥ|| 55|| patati| vāsudevaḥ
body.translated_text: Because of the offense of my son, O wielder of <s>Śārṅga</s>, to you — this is my head, O Lord of the Thirty gods, fallen at your feet! (Verse 55) (He falls.) <s>Vāsudeva</s>:
Alas, shame! The venerable one has fallen! Rise, rise!
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:

body.text: anugṛhīto.asmi| bhagavan idamarghyaṃ pādyaṃ ca pratigṛhyatām|
body.translated_text: I am favored! O Blessed One, please accept this welcome-offering (<s>arghya</s>) and foot-water (<s>pādya</s>).
<s>Vāsudeva</s>:

body.text: sarvaṃ gṛhṇāmi| kiṃ te bhūyaḥ priyamupaharāmi|
body.translated_text: I accept everything. What further pleasure may I render you?
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:
If the Lord is pleased with me, what more could I desire?
<s>Vāsudeva</s>:
Go now, until we meet again.
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:
As Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> commands.

body.text:
niṣkrāntaḥ| bharatavākyam| imāṃ sāgaraparyantāṃ himavadvindhyakuṇḍalām|
mahīmekātapatrāṅkāṃ rājasiṃhaḥ praśāstu naḥ|| 56|| niṣkrāntāḥ sarve| dūtavākyaṃ
samāptam|
ka iti| tricaraṇātikrāntatriloko
nārāyaṇaḥ khalvatra bhagavān| śaraṇaṃ vrajantu bhavantaḥ| yāvadga
body.translated_text: Exit. Benedictory verse: May the lion among kings rule for us this earth, girdled by the ocean, adorned with the earrings of the <s>Himālaya</s> and <s>Vindhya</s>, marked with the emblem of a single royal umbrella! (Verse 56) All exit. The <s>Dūtavākya</s> is concluded.
